benefits: Three-year working contract as an employee of the Institut Pasteur
A monthly salary of 2.000 EUR comprehensive of social benefits (national health care, health insurance, etc.)
A 'welcome bonus' of 4.000 EUR gross, paid at once with the first salary

Reimbursement of one round-trip ticket per year (train or plane, eco-class) to the country of origin: up to 1.300 EUR for non-continental European countries, up to 350 EUR for continental European countries
750 EUR per year per student to cover expenses related to attending international conferences or summer courses

Assistance with accommodation for the first year, one-to-one meetings with the Dean of the PPU, administrative and HR support, and access to Institut Pasteur and university amenities at reduced fees (cafeteria, ASIP sports, cultural rebates, free WiFi, free access to the Center for Scientific Information)
eligibility: Master degree or an equivalent university degree in science, medicine or related fields delivered by a university located outside France, by the time the students begin the programme (PPU-Classic, PPU-OXFORD, PPU-EID, PPU-Imagine)

Students holding a B.A. or a B.S. acquired after four years of academic education may be considered if they have additional laboratory experience of at least 6 months, with a written final report or a publication

Students who have already begun doctoral training elsewhere and students with a master's degree obtained in France are not eligible for these programmes; the candidate's nationality does not affect their eligibility

Students should not have resided in France for more than 12 months in the three years immediately prior to the application deadline (compulsory national service and short stays such as holidays are not taken into account)
The PPU doctoral programme does not have an age restriction; most accepted candidates are 24-26 years old and start their Ph.D. within a year of finishing their M.S., a few within 3 years

To present a candidate, thesis advisors must hold an HDR diploma; the host laboratory must be affiliated to the Institut Pasteur Paris and the research team to a doctoral school of any Parisian university (Universite Paris Cite, Sorbonne Universite, Universite Paris-Saclay)

Select up to four host-laboratory projects during the call and contact the potential host laboratories
Upload a detailed CV and a motivation letter in PDF format through the platform

No application through email will be accepted

Motivation letter in PDF format uploaded on the PPU platform
Copy of the Master's diploma or a certified written attestation of completion, available before the start of the programme (October)
Any additional information the advisor requests, which may include reference letters

Evaluation of the joint applications by the Admission Committee in December on academic qualifications, previous research experience, scientific potential of the candidate and adequation of the candidate with the proposed project
Four-day interview week at Institut Pasteur in February, scored on presentation, addressing the questions (comprehension, scientific and technical knowledge) and general attitude
Applicants are in general expected to be among the top of those qualified to enter a Ph.D. programme in their home country
Around 15 openings are available each year; admission is highly competitive and a waiting list is maintained
coverage: A monthly salary of 2.000 EUR comprehensive of social benefits (national health care, health insurance, etc.)
A 'welcome bonus' of 4.000 EUR gross paid with the first salary

Reimbursement of one round-trip ticket per year to the country of origin for the duration of the programme: up to 1.300 EUR for non-continental European countries, up to 350 EUR for continental European countries
750 EUR per year per student for expenses related to attending international conferences or summer courses
Assistance in accommodation for the first year (the rent itself is paid by the student)
Travel expenses (economy fare) and housing during the February interview week are paid by the PPU programme
application_method: Register on the PPU platform and select up to four host-laboratory projects
Upload a detailed CV and a motivation letter in PDF format
Be chosen by one host laboratory, then complete and upload the joint application with that laboratory on the same platform in November
If shortlisted, attend the four-day interview week at Institut Pasteur in February (travel and housing covered by the programme)
Notify the PPU of acceptance within the 10 days generally given to successful candidates
official.application_route: Online only through the PPU platform at ppu.pasteur.fr: the candidate applies to up to four labs, and the single selected lab then completes and uploads the joint application with the candidate; email applications are not accepted and there is no application fee
official.study_mode: Full-time, as an Institut Pasteur employee on a three-year working contract
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality restriction and no country-specific requirements for international applicants. However, the Master's degree must be awarded by a university located outside France, and the candidate must not have resided in France for more than 12 months in the three years immediately prior to the application deadline (PPU-Classic, PPU-OXFORD, PPU-EID, PPU-Imagine).
official.international_eligibility: International students are the intended population: PPU-Classic, PPU-OXFORD, PPU-EID and PPU-Imagine require a Master's degree from a university located outside France, with no geographical restriction on origin. The PPU-Research & Technology and PPU-Participatory Science tracks are open to any candidate holding a French or international Master's degree, and PPU-MD-PhD is open to medical doctors in cycle 2 or 3 of their training.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Life sciences and/or medical sciences: Molecular and Cellular Biology, Genetics, Immunology, Microbiology, Genomics, Bioinformatics, Structural Biology, Enzymology and Metabolism, Biological Chemistry, Virology, Parasitology, Medical Mycology, Epidemiology, Infectiology, Imaging, Neurosciences, Developmental Biology and Systems Biology. The thesis advisor must hold an HDR and the host laboratory must be affiliated with Institut Pasteur Paris and a doctoral school of a partner university.
official.research_requirement: The candidate must present Master's degree research (results or in progress) and the proposed Ph.D. project to the Admission Committee during the interview week; advisors may request reference letters and interview candidates by video conference during the first stage.
official.duration: Three years, starting in October 2027; students are expected to finish their Ph.D. in three years and the PPU programme only provides funding for three years
official.description: The Institut Pasteur organises this international doctoral programme with Universite Paris Cite, Sorbonne Universite and Universite Paris Saclay for students holding a Master's degree or equivalent in science, medicine and related fields. Selected students are employees of the Institut Pasteur on a three-year working contract, receive a monthly salary and conduct their research in one of the 150+ Institut Pasteur laboratories before defending a PhD according to European guidelines.
official.program_type: Doctoral salary contract (Ph.D. employment) at Institut Pasteur
official.english_requirement: The programme is run in English and therefore fluency in English is required; TOEFL or other language proficiency scores are not necessary but may be indicated when submitting the application. No knowledge of French is required, although a basic knowledge may be useful in daily life outside the institute, and French language courses are part of the curriculum.

applicant_utility.summary: PPU 2027 is an employment contract rather than a scholarship: you are hired by the Institut Pasteur on a three-year contract paying 2,000 EUR per month plus a 4,000 EUR gross welcome bonus, an annual home-trip reimbursement and 750 EUR a year for conferences. You cannot get in on your own application alone - a single Institut Pasteur laboratory must pick you as its only candidate before the joint file goes to the Admission Committee and the four-day February interview week. The call window is 1 October to 16 November 2026 for an October 2027 start, and your Master's may still be unfinished as long as the diploma or a certified attestation is in hand before then.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A final-year or newly graduated life- or medical-sciences Master's student from outside France with real laboratory experience, who can win over one Institut Pasteur supervisor and stays inside the 12-month France residency limit.
application_readiness_checklist: Create the ppu.pasteur.fr account as soon as the call opens on 1 October 2026 and read all 2027 project descriptions before contacting anyone
Contact four to six supervisors early with a short project-specific email and an up-to-date CV; ask what extra material each wants (reference letters, transcripts, a video call)
Keep a CV and motivation letter ready as separate PDFs that can be tailored per project rather than one generic text
Verify your France-residency record for the last three years before investing months in the process - more than 12 months disqualifies the classic tracks
Plan to have the Master's diploma or a certified attestation of completion ready for the October 2027 start, and expect a 10-day acceptance window after offers
common_rejection_risks: Each advisor may present only one candidate, so a strong application still loses if a rival candidate secures that laboratory first
A CV and motivation letter that are not tailored to the specific project read poorly when the joint application is scored on 'adequation of the candidate with the proposed project'
Weak answers on your own Master's research or on the proposed Ph.D. project during the February interview week, which is scored on comprehension and handling of open questions
Being ruled out by a mobility rule: more than 12 months' residence in France in the previous three years, a Master's awarded in France, or doctoral training already started elsewhere
Applying to far fewer than four laboratories and therefore having no fallback when labs choose other candidates
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Rent for your Paris accommodation (the Cite Internationale Universitaire de Paris room offered on arrival is paid by the student), the gap between a 2,000 EUR Paris salary and real living costs, visa and relocation costs beyond the 4,000 EUR one-off bonus, and any support for a spouse or family, which the programme explicitly does not provide. Thesis extensions beyond year three are not financed by PPU.
applicant_utility.document_audit: Both the CV and the motivation letter must be PDFs, and nothing sent by email counts as an application, so anything mailed directly to a laboratory is supplementary only. Reference letters are requested at each advisor's discretion, so secure them early rather than at interview stage. The Master's diploma or certified attestation must exist before the October 2027 start even though you apply while still finishing the degree.
applicant_utility.alerts: The programme page mixes generic 'call opens in September' wording with the 2027 banner dates, so rely on the 1 October - 16 November 2026 window and re-check the page before the deadline. Interview week falls in February with results within about a week and only ~10 days to accept, so decide your priorities in advance. Roughly 15 places exist per year across six PPU tracks, and holding an external fellowship does not exempt you from the same selection process.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You register on the PPU platform and apply to up to four laboratories alone; the laboratory that selects you completes and uploads the joint application with you on the same platform; the Admission Committee reviews everything in December; shortlisted candidates travel to Paris for a four-day February interview week.

applicant_utility.summary: InLife's 2026-2027 incoming mobility grant is a 7,500 EUR one-off for a Master's student from a foreign university to take up a research stay in a Sorbonne University Alliance laboratory, intended to cover travel and housing while the host arrangement pays the usual Master 2 internship stipend. The decisive detail is that students cannot apply themselves: InLife states plainly that the call is addressed to host laboratories and that direct applications from Master's students will not be considered, so your effective entry point is a supervisor willing to write the file with you. The whole dossier is one PDF - project leader CV, candidate CV and grades, and a one-page project description - emailed to InLife by 2 November 2026 at 18:00.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A Master 2 student at a foreign university with strong grades and an existing or budding collaboration with a Paris-area lab in the life-sciences interface, whose future supervisor is willing to drive the application.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify a lab affiliated with Sorbonne Universite, MNHN, UTC or CNAM that works at the interface of life sciences with your topic, and approach the supervisor weeks before 2 November 2026
Agree with the lab that the project genuinely qualifies as interdisciplinary at the interface of fields related to the study of living systems, since that is the stated admissibility test
Prepare your CV and grade records, with class ranking if your university publishes one, compressed to one page each
Co-write the one-page project description: 5 keywords, context, questions, approaches, the interdisciplinary dimension, and whether it extends an active or new collaboration with a foreign laboratory
State explicitly in the project description if InLife should also fund the Master 2 stipend, because that request must appear in this document
Merge everything into a single PDF and email it to initiative-inlife@sorbonne-universite.fr before 18:00 on 2 November 2026
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the application yourself as a student, which InLife excludes outright
A project that reads as single-discipline rather than interdisciplinary at the interface of the study of living systems
Overrunning the page limits - the project description is one page and the CVs are one page each, and the file is judged as one package
A host laboratory that belongs to an institution outside the Sorbonne University Alliance
Failing to request stipend funding in the project description, leaving the Master 2 internship stipend unfunded and the stay financially unviable
Missing the 18:00 cut-off on 2 November 2026 because the supervisor only received the file at the last minute
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition is not mentioned anywhere in the call, and beyond travel and accommodation the grant does not pay daily living costs; the value of the Master 2 internship stipend for 2026-2027 is not published, so the student must budget for that gap independently. The award is a one-off rather than a monthly allowance, so it cannot carry a long stay on its own.
applicant_utility.document_audit: Only one PDF is accepted, so nothing can be added after submission. The candidate's grades are requested 'if possible with rankings', so a missing ranking is a visible weakness rather than a formality. The 5 key words and the active-or-new collaboration statement are compulsory content. Note that the call does not ask for a motivation letter, so do not substitute one for the required project description.
applicant_utility.alerts: The call is run for host laboratories, so the practical deadline is whenever your supervisor has time to write the file - start several weeks before 2 November 2026. Only three mobility grants exist for the entire 2026-2027 year, and InLife's Master 2 internship call shares the same 2 November 2026, 18:00 deadline, which creates competition for supervisor attention. The English and French pages were both updated on 7 October 2026, so re-check for revisions before submitting.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: The host laboratory emails a single PDF containing the project leader's CV, the candidate's CV and grades, and a one-page project description to InLife; the InLife Executive Committee evaluates the file and awards the grant for the incoming student's stay.
